text:
cory: quick sync — hitting weird tail latency on 8xA100 runs when we route KV cache for hot prefixes across TP slices. Perf numbers look like comm spikes during middle pipeline stages. anyone seen this pattern?

maya: saw something similar last week. spikes line up with our all-reduce timeouts when sequence_len ~ 900 and batch inter-arrival jitter > 20ms. not sure if kernel selection is falling back to slower path.

noah: profiling dump attached from last friday run (shortened):
```
TIMING SUMMARY
stage 2: compute 12ms, comm(all-reduce) 34ms, idle 6ms
stage 3: compute 14ms, comm 36ms, idle 4ms
KV fetch (shard 3->5): 28ms (includes point-to-point + barrier)
```
Looks like comm dominates when KV fetches cross TP boundaries.

leo: +1. Also noticed when we shard KV by DP-friendly hashing (round-robin across GPUs) we get worse overlap than when KV is colocated with TP ranks handling attention heads. Basically locality wins for those hot prefixes.

cory: so two orthogonal knobs: where KV shards live (placement) and runtime batching heuristics. If a request's prefix hits a KV shard on a different PP stage, we force sync.

maya: thought: what if we bias the batching window to prefer co-located prefixes? Eg: hierarchical batching key = (model_version, tp_group, prefix_cluster). If we detect hot prefix -> hold for up to 10ms to gather co-located requests. reduces cross-node P2P calls.

noah: that helps throughput but risks latency SLO. our SLO is 95th < 120ms. Holding 10ms might be OK if overall tail drops. we should simulate on trace.

leo: kernel selection note: for sequences > 800, the fused-kernel path (v2) uses an all-reduce-friendly schedule; for shorter sequences we use unrolled kernels that don't overlap well with NVLink. We might be choosing unrolled paths because batch shapes vary after batching heuristics.

perf-bot: nightly-profile: 2026-06-08 02:10UTC 
- baseline: all-reduce avg 21ms
- current: all-reduce avg 35ms (std 8ms)
- top offenders: shard 3->5 traffic (42% of cross-gpu bytes)

maya: suggestion: two experiments: (A) pin KV shards to TP groups (co-locate with attention compute) and enable conservative batching (hold 8ms for matching tp_group requests). (B) keep DP-distributed shards but force kernel v2 for sequence_len >= 512 via override flag so kernel generates more overlap.

cory: nice. expected tradeoffs?

noah: A should reduce P2P volume and barrier stalls, but could create hotspot GPU memory usage and uneven load. B increases compute overlap but might regress memory footprint and increase single-GPU latency for some requests.

leo: quick back-of-envelope from trace sampling: co-locating reduces cross-shard bytes by ~58% on hot prefixes, which should cut comm time by ~30-40% assuming same network BW.

maya: I'll run a small 8-GPU experiment with synthetic hot-prefix traffic: 70% of requests hit 10 hot prefixes, rest random. Will measure p50/p95/p99 and per-stage all-reduce time.

cory: add a metric for KV fetch hop count (local, intra-node, inter-node). Also capture kernel path chosen per request (v1/v2).

noah: also add a regression check: if forcing kernel v2 increases p99 compute by >10% we should abort that variant.

leo: implementation note: routing table change for A will require changes in shard-coordinator: add affinity weight for tp_group and an eviction policy to avoid OOM on hotspots.

maya: plan posted: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kv-hotspot-experiments (draft) — will push configs to test cluster 8-GPU and 32-GPU.

cory: action items:
- maya: run experiments A + B and collect traces (due EOD tomorrow)
- noah: add kernel-path tagging to profiler and KV hop-count metric (today)
- leo: prototype shard affinity eviction (start today)

noah: one more thing — if we do affinity, we should also add randomizing fallback for cold prefixes so we don't end up with long tail on cold requests that get rehashed to busy GPUs.

cory: agreed. last note: watch out for mixed-precision quant kernels — they sometimes pick reduced-allreduce implementations that look faster in isolation but have poor scaling at scale. keep an eye on perf-bot logs.

maya: thanks all — will report results in this thread. :thumbsup:
